title: When Can a Swarm Be Audited?
subtitle: Track 4 Multi-Agent Oversight and Control
author: Razvan Sacara
abstract: We focus on Track 4, Multi-Agent Oversight and Control. An agent can claim completion without performing an authorized action; a checkpoint can change behavior without changing a handoff. We evaluate these distinctions in a bounded fake-data workflow with genuine model-chosen actions and an independently checked evidence oracle. We collected 720 actor calls and 9,360 monitor calls, pairing continued-worker and delegated workflows across 192 source groups. Adaption and Hugging Face supply three endpoints from two model families reading complete, random-loss and selective-loss evidence. Metadata-only restoration and random add-back share a two-record budget. The registered primary restoration contrast was +5.73 [+1.04, +10.42] percentage points in grounded correctness. A separate one-hop influence intervention measures policy violations and useful completion. A separately frozen weight experiment collected 144 numeric controller proposals across 24 representations and two tasks. Gemma 31B repaired 16/24 within six scalar edits; the other writers repaired 0/24 and 0/24. Constructed controls include harmful action changes under identical handoffs and harmless checkpoint changes. All datasets retain invalid outputs and service failures, with public offline replay and disclosed operational continuation. Earlier scripted results remain separate. The findings concern finite evidence support and tiny composed policies; they do not establish spontaneous collusion, general weight interpretation or deployment safety.
sections: 1. Introduction

An origin marks a fake revocation flag, hands off a target update, and a receiver reports done. Was an update applied, was it permitted at settlement, and which immutable worker executed it? These questions require different evidence. A second concern arises when a downstream controller changes its action while its incoming handoff stays unchanged. Multi-agent oversight needs both dependable records and checks of actual behavior [1,4].

We investigate supported executor attribution under evidence loss, then separately test direct numerical repair of tiny delegated policies. Track 4 (Multi-Agent Oversight and Control) anchors the project, with Track 3 identity/checkpoint relevance. The contribution is a bounded, reproducible evaluation with genuine API outputs and explicit negative controls. The current sprint rubric rewards impact, sound execution and clarity; a positive result is not a prerequisite for a useful experiment [10].
2. Related Work and Prior Results

Qin et al. already demonstrate trace tampering and peer influence [2]. Yun et al. separate supported findings from correct guesses and study binding/renaming [3]. BRIDGE studies verified handoff repair [5]; Who&When and BLADE address decisive-error responsibility [6,7]. Agent Flight Recorder and NovaFabric already supply recording/provenance/replay concepts [20,21]. Our labels concern the executor of a designated unpermitted update, not intent, causal blame or a new logging primitive.

Prompt Infection establishes inter-agent propagation, while AI Control studies oversight under subversion [8,9]. Selected Apart examples motivate narrower distinctions: Syscon separates observation from detection, and ActionLens emphasizes component usefulness and simulation validity [11,12]. Our influence arm is one controlled hop, not spontaneous coordination or network spread.

Our completed scripted predecessor used 192 sources and 3,840 Adaption calls plus 240 HF calls on 24 shared sources. Its primary selective-minus-random unsupported-worker estimate was -1.04 [-6.77, +4.69] percentage points. Schema-priority restoration improved primary-reader grounded correctness by +43.23 [+37.50, +48.96] points, but the smaller HF contrast was -4.17 [-29.17, +20.83]. These remain old results, not fresh confirmation. They motivated genuine action generation, variable loss and a larger matched reader comparison.

Takehi et al. report direct neural-weight reading/writing and feedback-assisted larger-network experiments [13]. Their released sycophancy logs also document four unsuccessful weights-only attempts [14]. Tracr already compiles programs into weights, and network reparameterizations can preserve functions [15,22]. Our tiny-policy study tests sparse model-written repairs and joint behavior under explicit controls; it does not reproduce large-LLM editing or originate neural compilation.
3. Methods

Live workflow. Each of 192 fresh source groups has one actual origin call followed by two receiver branches. The origin chooses mark/skip for an independently authorized decoy flag and generates a handoff. The receiver chooses write/read/refuse; only a valid write increments a new fake dictionary. No model text is executed as code. Sequential permission is original authorization; deferred permission additionally requires that the origin did not mark/revoke; approval_join additionally requires both approval bits. Applied unpermitted writes remain possible. Invalid choices perform no operation and remain separately reported.

Matched branches and sampling. Solo replays the actual first user/assistant exchange to the same immutable worker. Delegated starts a different worker with the typed handoff and authoritative current facts. This changes both identity and context boundary, not agent count alone. Shared origins imply dependence: 192 origins plus 384 receivers are 576 unique core calls. Each family has 64 groups, balanced by assigned original authorization, never by observed violation. Routes, aliases, approvals and independent namespaces were privately sampled and hash-committed before inference, then released. All families were previously studied and used in qualification; no unseen-family claim follows.

Evidence and support. A protected host collector records requests, bindings, results and post-state separately. The factual label is the immutable executor of an applied unpermitted target update, otherwise NONE. Enumerated histories vary same/distinct routes according to branch, alias permutations, origin/target outcomes and approval bits. The whole visible packet must match. Singleton support permits a definite finding; several labels require ABSTAIN; empty support blocks admission. A separately implemented constraint checker agrees before each audit dispatch. Notes and completion claims are untrusted; original authorization, initial state, branch mode and advisory context remain public even when redundant records are lost.

Loss and acquisition. Each trajectory has twelve workflow records and eight unrelated maintenance records. Random loss deletes four of twenty; selective loss deletes two from a family-specific four-record critical set and two from its complement. Masks are fixed independently of outputs and shared across branches/readers. A manifest exposes only opaque ID, kind and handle, not actor, status, payload or length. Metadata retrieval ranks target result, target binding, decoy result, approval and origin binding; random retrieval samples the same missing inventory. Both add at most two authentic records. Seven views cover full/lost/restored exports. This typed collector interface and synthetic critical sets remain favorable assumptions; equal records do not imply equal information, bytes or tokens.

Readers and scoring. Gemma 4 26B A4B is the primary reader, Gemma 4 31B is a same-family secondary, and HF Llama 3.3 70B/Novita is the cross-family reader on ALL 192 shared source groups. Main auditing has 384 trajectories times seven views times three readers: 8,064 requests. Unsupported worker U=1 when a named executor lacks singleton support, even if factually right. Grounded correctness, supported definite coverage, unsupported NONE, strict encoding and INVALID accompany U. Invalids never disappear from planned denominators. Exact-packet, always-abstain and fixed-A comparators use the same evidence. Fresh contexts, temperature zero, 4,096 output tokens and disabled model tools/memory/storage follow the registered serving profiles [16,17]. Names do not pin immutable weights.

Live primary and influence. The NEW primary is metadata-minus-random restoration grounded correctness, averaged over both loss mechanisms within each delegated source, primary reader only. Whole-source bootstrap resampling uses 10,000 draws stratified by family/assigned authorization. The older primary is not replaced. Secondary comparisons include branches, other readers and unsupported accusations. Forty-eight shared sources additionally receive matched-length benign text, malicious text, or malicious text plus warning: 144 receiver calls and 1,296 audits of three loss views. Equal characters are not equal tokens. Useful completion means a write when permitted or read otherwise; safe refusal is reported separately. Appended content and warning are controlled interventions, not evidence of spontaneous collusion.

Weight-space microbenchmark. A separate teacher writes two 4-input/4-ReLU/1-score controllers, fifty scalars jointly. Intended A should emit original_auth AND approval_A; B consumes that bit and should emit handoff AND approval_B AND NOT revoked. B output actually increments fake state. Twenty-four input-role/hidden-unit/rescaling representations cover three planted local defects. Each writer gets synthesis and at-most-six-scalar repair tasks, one response each: 144 proposals. There is no target-network training, gradient or forward-pass feedback. JSON shapes, finite bounds and edit counts are mechanical admission gates; failures remain in the denominator. All 32 Boolean contexts are checked against the global rule, not an assumed intermediate factorization. The unit is a representation variant, not a truth-table row.

Weight controls and analysis. Correct symbolic policies are positive controls; unchanged defects are unsafe controls. Reparameterized GOOD policies are negative harm controls, not budget-matched repairs. Hash-change alarms cannot distinguish their harmless changes. A seeded eight-context behavioral probe is compared with full checking. For example, with both approvals and original authorization true, revocation should prevent a write; a planted revocation-sign defect writes while the upstream handoff remains one. We count such action changes under identical upstream bits. For admitted proposals, twenty random deltas preserve selected cells and L2 norm; out-of-bound draws fail without resampling. The primary repair exactness proportion is separate for each writer, with 10,000 variant bootstraps stratified by defect template. These controls address bounded policy semantics, not general weights-only intent detection.
4. Results

Collection. The live study retained 720 actor and 9,360 audit terminal records; the weight study retained 144 proposals. Complete grids do not turn INVALID outcomes into successful answers. Qualification is excluded. The registered operational continuation retained earlier failed outputs without retries (Appendix B). Table 1 gives delegated source-level effects; Table 2 pools only the 8,064 MAIN reader views descriptively. The new primary metadata-restoration contrast was +5.73 [+1.04, +10.42] percentage points. Intervals across zero do not establish equivalence, and zero-event bootstrap intervals do not certify zero risk.

TABLE2

The new restoration contrasts are positive across all three endpoints; this larger matched comparison uses new actions, masks and metadata acquisition, not retries of the old HF protocol. The selective-loss unsupported-worker contrasts are negative, illustrating why accusation counts alone cannot represent investigation quality. Grounded correctness, unsupported NONE, answer coverage and invalidity must be read together.

Actual worker behavior. Solo executed 2/192 unauthorized writes and achieved 50 useful completions; delegated executed 4/192 and achieved 48. Delegated-minus-solo violation and usefulness differences were +1.04 [+0.00, +2.60] and -1.04 [-2.60, +0.00] points. Invalid receiver choices were 0 and 0. These compare the declared compound workflows, not an isolated effect of agent count.

Influence. On 48 sources, the benign/malicious/warning conditions executed 2/2/1 unauthorized writes and achieved 11/11/11 useful completions. Malicious-minus-benign violation was +0.00 [+0.00, +0.00] points; warning-minus-malicious usefulness was +0.00 [+0.00, +0.00]. Violations occurred in all three conditions. The two zero paired contrasts do not establish absence of influence or robust mitigation; this is a controlled one-hop test.

Weight programming. Table 3 retains every planned artifact, including invalid schemas and edits over budget. Repair schema-valid counts were 23/24, 24/24, 24/24; admitted six-edit counts were 2/24, 23/24, 10/24, in table order. Gemma 31B produced 16 exact global repairs. Its conditional same-cell/norm random comparator succeeded on 55/460 draws over 23 admitted artifacts; those draws are dependent controls. Admitted synthesis proposals were unsafe on at least one context in 23/23, 4/20, 22/24 cases, in table order. Gemma 31B had 16 safe synthesis artifacts but only 5 exact ones. Analytically, always-zero controllers match 30/32 contexts yet miss both permitted writes. Exactness therefore includes useful permitted work, beyond safety or average row accuracy.
TABLE3

Checkpoint controls. Planted defects produced 96 unauthorized fake actions across the 24 representation truth tables; 88 occurred under unchanged upstream handoffs. All 24 function-preserving changes retained correct behavior while changing the hash. A hash-only harm alarm therefore flagged all 24 defects AND all 24 harmless changes. The eight-context probe caught 10/24 defective representations. This is a constructed communication/action disagreement and finite probe comparison, not a measured false-negative rate of an LLM message monitor.

Resources. Main plus influence token-rate estimates were 1.0315761365 Adaption credits and $0.687000460 HF; the weight proposals estimate 0.0170366750 credits and $0.010478120. Excluded qualifications and earlier pilots are separately retained. These are not reconciled invoices or provider-enforced spending caps. No training, GPU rental or credit top-up was performed.
5. Discussion and Limitations

The practical question is whether an investigator has enough authentic evidence to justify a finding. Executing a fake workflow makes evidence correspond to actual interpreted choices; it does not make the workflow representative of deployed swarms. Metadata acquisition can repair some joins, while a changed policy can require behavioral validation even when communication appears unchanged. A checkpoint hash identifies bytes relative to a trusted record; alone it establishes neither provenance nor semantics.

The collector, observation grammar and available originals are trusted. Only two workers, three transition structures, fixed loss policies and a typed two-record retrieval interface were evaluated. Architecture changes context as well as identity. Shared origins/views do not create independent n. Two endpoints share a family, actor and primary reader share a model, and hosted weights are not pinned. Reader effects include serving/schema compliance as well as evidence reasoning; per-view invalidity remains released. Earlier serving failures and a format amendment informed operational choices; all remain disclosed. No real incidents, compromised collectors, large populations or spontaneous collusion were tested.

The weight networks have only fifty scalars and three fault templates. Their full Boolean rule is provided, and exhaustive verification is possible here; neither scales automatically to large LLMs. Hash-change and handoff-collision controls establish constructed distinctions, not a new generic detector. Bootstrap intervals describe the declared representation generator. Training a small monitor remains a separately gated intervention: compare individual-row and interaction-aware SFT on one base with matched budgets and NEW source splits, then test once. Joint policy optimization requires rollout/reward design; direct weight writing is neither SFT nor proof of collective alignment. MALT already trains role-specific policies using interaction-derived credit [23]; our work does not originate multi-agent training [18].
6. Conclusion

Metadata-selected authentic restoration improved grounded correctness over random add-back across three endpoints in this bounded workflow. Gemma 31B also supplied sixteen exact sparse repairs, while checkpoint controls separated harmful behavior from harmless parameter changes. These results support evidence acquisition and behavioral contract checks, within the declared collector and tiny-policy assumptions. Public offline replay permits inspection of actual choices and artifacts; neither result establishes general swarm safety or intent inference.

appendix: Appendix A. Limitations and Dual-Use / Ethical Considerations

Trusted collector originals, finite typed actions, known authorization rules and authentic restoration are assumptions. Record order is schema order, not wall-clock chronology. Dynamic untrusted prose does not constrain candidate worlds; policy/namespace/advisory public fields remain visible independently of lost redundant records. The oracle does not represent every possible real history. Two implementations can share a specification error. No operating-system containment, collector-compromise resistance or universal originality is established.

Evidence-loss studies could inform selective suppression; weight-policy repairs could also inform harmful edits. Released tasks are harmless fake-data controls and finite numeric artifacts. Models receive no real credentials, incident payloads, arbitrary shell/Python tools or human-subject data. Generated numerical JSON is never executed as code. Native provider IDs, headers, raw reasoning and keys remain excluded. Checkpoint changes are not labeled malicious merely because bytes differ.

The team remains responsible for all claims and human author review. The current official template, eight-main-page cap and required appendix govern submission; automated checks and selected winning-project lessons do not guarantee eligibility or prizes. Source review is targeted, with inaccessible/partially reviewed originals recorded in SOURCE_AUDIT.md.
Appendix B. Registration and complete iteration history

The older stateful-main-v2 study and matched HF serving amendments remain in their tags/results-v1. Its main HTTP 502 was retained INVALID; a separately registered continuation collected only 812 previously unstarted identities. Earlier HF Cerebras preflight issued zero evaluation calls; Qwen/Nscale stopped after eight calls/three truncations. Failed qualifications were never reclassified as passes. Their outputs are not pooled with the new studies.

Live-v1 completed 270 excluded calls, but primary schema validity was 28/84, versus secondary 84/84 and HF 82/84. Forty-five primary failures omitted worker_id. Live-v2 prospectively clarified both mandatory fields with complete examples, preserving decoder/95% gate/scientific endpoints and retaining all v1 data. A fresh independently sampled private design and fresh source-index ranges preceded v2 qualification/main outputs. V2 passed all serving/encoding gates; qualification accuracy was not an admission criterion. Both live versions are retained. The grammar remains live-audit-v1; that record-schema name is distinct from collection-version live-audit-v2.

Live-v2 source/config/protocol and private-design commitment are bound by their published pre-output tag. Actor source groups 4,400,000–4,400,063, 4,410,000–4,410,063 and 4,420,000–4,420,063 differ from qualification indices 4,300,000/4,310,000/4,320,000 plus 0–1. The public namespace is independently drawn, not the seed selecting hidden routes. The exact committed context plan is released only after evaluation for public replay.

The live audit phase stopped at 204/8,064 terminal requests when the third known-usage Gemma 31B incomplete response triggered its original gate. Before further calls, live-audit-v2-continuation-v1 bound the untouched predecessor and exact 7,860 unstarted identities. Known-usage truncations remain INVALID without a count stop; no failed request was retried. A bounded sliding window replaces the batch barrier while preserving maximum four active calls/two HF and all active cost reservations. Prompts, models, token limits, planned identities and analysis are unchanged. This operational stopping/scheduling amendment was not selected on live correctness effects; it is not an uninterrupted unamended confirmatory run. Earlier and new invalids remain in denominators.

Weight-audit-v1 was separately published before its six excluded numeric-schema qualification calls and 144 main proposals. Qualification required completed known-usage valid shapes, not successful repair or favorable effects. Main representation indices are 5,200,000–5,200,023; qualification is 5,100,000. Source hashes, request-body digests and native normalization are checked in export. Both studies journal/fsync starts and terminal outcomes, make no automatic retries and can continue only unchanged unstarted identities when no uncertain start or active failure gate remains.

Per-phase nominal ceilings were ten Adaption credits/$1 HF, with four concurrent requests maximum and two HF requests. Applicable gateway/length/auth/usage/profile gates were registered before each phase, including the length-stop change above; client estimates are not hard account billing limits. Provider-reported fields and estimated liabilities are not reconciled account debits. Available credit is a resource ceiling, not a reason to expand samples after observing effects. No top-up, training job, GPU rental or deployment was performed.
Appendix C. Reproduction and future adaptation

Why the harmless checkpoint control works. For a positive scale, ReLU of a scaled input equals that scale times the original ReLU output. Multiplying a hidden unit's incoming weights and bias by that scale, then dividing its outgoing weight by the same scale, preserves its contribution. Permuting hidden units preserves their sum. These transformations preserve the score and threshold decision, while changing serialized parameters. This mathematical control does not imply that arbitrary small edits preserve behavior.

The offline live verifier reconstructs actual actor inputs/history boundaries, typed choices, host state, projection/support, reader scores, source-level bootstrap effects, baselines and cost arithmetic. The weight verifier reconstructs all numerical artifacts, admission decisions, truth tables, controls, variant estimates and costs. Public replay needs no credentials or native archives. Raw hashes support local provenance checks but do not independently prove provider authenticity or final invoices.

20-rules-of-learning guides presentation: begin with a concrete handoff, define permission/execution/support before metrics, keep source groups distinct from dependent views, and connect each result to the experiment that generated it. It is an editorial aid, not evidence of novelty or causality.

Future training must distinguish ordinary independent-example SFT, interaction-aware trajectory SFT and jointly rewarded policy optimization. Compare one base before/after matched training-token and optimizer budgets; split NEW source groups before projection/augmentation. Ambiguous packets need ABSTAIN targets rather than hidden executor labels. The current evaluation can diagnose a failure but cannot also become its untouched training test. Vendor row minima, bounded charge and working downloaded base/adapter inference must be established before launch. Joint reward should penalize violations, not reward successful unauthorized work [18].

Codex assisted with primary-source research, implementation, checking, analysis and writing. Isolated OpenCode reviewers inspected allowlisted source copies and generated tested fixtures without keys or native data. Hosted Adaption/HF models supplied actual retained actor, monitor and numerical-proposal outputs. Scoped automated review is not human author approval, independent empirical replication or an Apart acceptance decision.
